litigation.mdlName: In re: Aqueous Film-Forming Foams Products Liability Litigation
litigation.court: U.S. District Court, District of South Carolina (Charleston)

phase: 3M personal-injury agreement and claimant identification; separate water-system settlements
phaseDetail: Under CMO 39, counsel must identify eligible clients, including eligible unfiled clients, by November 13, 2026. Eligible people already representing themselves in the MDL on covered personal-injury claims against 3M must identify themselves by the same date. Identification is the first step. The settlement election and claim package are separate. CMO 40 stays covered MDL proceedings as to 3M, subject to the procedures and exceptions in CMOs 39 and 40. The stay leaves claims against other defendants outside its scope.
defendants: Arkema, Chemguard, Buckeye Fire Equipment, National Foam, Dynax and others

settlements.label: 3M — personal-injury settlement agreement
settlements.detail: 3M signed a November 3, 2026 personal-injury agreement with a $7.35 billion nominal commitment through 2034, subject to participation thresholds. The agreement is separate from the public-water-system settlements and provides no fixed payout for every individual claimant.
settlements.individualClaims: Under CMO 39, counsel must identify eligible clients, including eligible unfiled clients, by November 13, 2026. Eligible people already representing themselves in the MDL on covered personal-injury claims against 3M must identify themselves by the same date. Identification is the first step. The settlement election and claim package are separate.

settlements.label: 3M — public water systems
settlements.status: final approved, claims administration — water systems only
settlements.detail: $10.5 billion to $12.5 billion paid over 13 years to public water systems for PFAS contamination, per the official settlement FAQ. Final approval entered by Judge Gergel (fairness hearing February 2, 2024). Compensates water utilities, not individuals.
settlements.individualClaims: Public water systems only; this settlement does not resolve individual personal-injury claims.

settlements.label: DuPont / Chemours / Corteva — public water systems
settlements.status: final approved, claims administration — water systems only
settlements.detail: $1.185 billion settlement resolving claims of roughly 14,000 public water systems. Final approval entered following the December 14, 2023 fairness hearing.
settlements.individualClaims: Public water systems only; this settlement does not resolve individual personal-injury claims.

settlements.label: Tyco Fire Products / Chemguard — public water systems
settlements.status: final approved, claims administration — water systems only
settlements.detail: $750 million settlement; final approval order entered November 2024 (ECF 6406).
settlements.individualClaims: Public water systems only; this settlement does not resolve individual personal-injury claims.

settlements.label: BASF — public water systems
settlements.status: final approved, claims administration — water systems only
settlements.detail: $316.5 million total ($312.5M settlement amount + $4M notice/administration); agreement signed May 20, 2024, final approval entered November 22, 2024.
settlements.source: BASF preliminary approval motion (official settlement site)
settlements.individualClaims: Public water systems only; this settlement does not resolve individual personal-injury claims.

settlements.label: Carrier, Amerex, Archroma and Nation Ford — proposed public-water-system settlements
settlements.detail: The administrator lists four additional proposed water-system settlements with preliminary approval. Its C.A.A.N. schedule lists objections due November 23, 2026, exclusion requests due December 22, 2026, and a final fairness hearing on January 15, 2027. These are not individual personal-injury programs.
settlements.individualClaims: Eligible public-water-system claims only; no individual personal-injury payment program is announced by these proposals.

updates.summary: 3M signed a November 3, 2026 personal-injury agreement with a $7.35 billion nominal commitment through 2034, subject to participation thresholds. The agreement is separate from the public-water-system settlements and provides no fixed payout for every individual claimant.

Under CMO 39, counsel must identify eligible clients, including eligible unfiled clients, by November 13, 2026. Eligible people already representing themselves in the MDL on covered personal-injury claims against 3M must identify themselves by the same date. Identification is the first step. The settlement election and claim package are separate.
CMO 40 stays covered MDL proceedings as to 3M, subject to the procedures and exceptions in CMOs 39 and 40. The stay leaves claims against other defendants outside its scope.
JPML reports 15,270 pending actions in MDL-2873 on November 2, 2026, up 6 from October 1; 19,846 total historical actions are reported separately.

The public-water-system administrator now lists four additional proposed C.A.A.N. settlements with preliminary approval; final fairness is scheduled for January 15, 2027. These proposals do not announce an individual personal-injury payment program.
CMO 4E clarifies limited disclosure of case-caption, plaintiff-name and alleged-exposure-source information for proceedings before the JPML. It does not announce a settlement or trial date.
JPML reports 15,264 pending actions in MDL-2873 on October 1, 2026, unchanged from 15,264 on September 1; 19,840 total historical actions are reported separately.
JPML reports 15,264 pending actions on September 1, 2026, compared with 15,246 on August 3; 19,840 total historical actions are reported separately.
CMO 26O moves Group B case-selection and expert-discovery proposals to November 20, 2026.
CMO 33F sets thyroid/liver-cancer expert-motion responses for November 20, 2026 and replies for January 22, 2027; it does not set a trial.
The administrator confirms four water-system settlements have final approval; the Phase Two water-system claims deadline was July 31, 2026.
